<a id="T030"></a>
## T030

- Date: 1991-03-01
- Place: Montreal, Canada
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Convention on the Marking of Plastic Explosives for the Purpose of Detection was concluded.

Summary: On 1 March 1991, the Convention on the Marking of Plastic Explosives for the Purpose of Detection was concluded in Montreal. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, parties must prohibit the manufacture and movement of unmarked plastic explosives and destroy or mark existing stocks within set periods. It follows Security Council resolution 635 (T028).

Citation: [CONV-PLASTIC1991](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-PLASTIC1991) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv10-english.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/Conv10-english.pdf))

<a id="T031"></a>
## T031

- Date: 1992-01-21
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Middle East/North Africa
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 731 (1992) concerning Libya and the Pan Am 103 and UTA 772 investigations.

Summary: On 21 January 1992, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 731 concerning Libya and the investigations into the destruction of Pan Am flight 103 and UTA flight 772. The Council condemned the destruction of the two aircraft and the loss of hundreds of lives. Sanctions followed in resolution 748 (T032).

Citation: [UNSC731](../sources/regions/middle-east-north-africa.md#UNSC731) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/731\(1992\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/731(1992)))

<a id="T032"></a>
## T032

- Date: 1992-03-31
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Middle East/North Africa
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 748 (1992) imposing measures on Libya.

Summary: On 31 March 1992, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 748, imposing measures on Libya. It required Libya to comply with the requests made under resolution 731 (T031) and to commit to cease all forms of terrorist action and assistance to terrorist groups.

Citation: [UNSC748](../sources/regions/middle-east-north-africa.md#UNSC748) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/748\(1992\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/748(1992)))

<a id="T033"></a>
## T033

- Date: 1993-02-26
- Place: New York, United States
- Region: North America
- Theme: major operations
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

A bomb exploded in the parking garage of the World Trade Center, according to the FBI's history page.

Summary: On 26 February 1993, a bomb exploded in the parking garage beneath the World Trade Center in New York, according to the FBI's history page. The FBI says it left a crater several stories deep and killed six people.

Citation: [FBI-WTC1993](../sources/regions/north-america.md#FBI-WTC1993) ([https://www.fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/world-trade-center-bombing-1993](https://www.fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/world-trade-center-bombing-1993))

<a id="T034"></a>
## T034

- Date: 1994-12-09
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 49/60 containing the Declaration on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism.

Summary: On 9 December 1994, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 49/60, containing the Declaration on Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism. In the Declaration, Member States reaffirm their unequivocal condemnation of all acts, methods and practices of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, wherever and by whomever committed.

Citation: [UNGA49-60](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNGA49-60) ([https://undocs.org/A/RES/49/60](https://undocs.org/A/RES/49/60))

<a id="T035"></a>
## T035

- Date: 1995-04-19
- Place: Oklahoma City, United States
- Region: North America
- Theme: major operations
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building was bombed; the FBI's history page records 168 deaths.

Summary: On 19 April 1995, the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City was destroyed by a truck bomb; the FBI's history page records 168 deaths. The FBI page names the convicted perpetrator, which CTA6 does not repeat here. Why the event matters beyond the deaths recorded is not stated in the cited source \[UNKNOWN\].

Citation: [FBI-OKC](../sources/regions/north-america.md#FBI-OKC) ([https://www.fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/oklahoma-city-bombing](https://www.fbi.gov/history/famous-cases/oklahoma-city-bombing))

<a id="T036"></a>
## T036

- Date: 1995-09-27
- Place: Strasbourg, France (European Court of Human Rights)
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in M. and Others v. the United Kingdom (no. 18984/91) concerning the 1988 Gibraltar shootings.

Summary: On 27 September 1995, the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in M. and Others v. the United Kingdom (no. 18984/91), concerning the 1988 Gibraltar shootings of three IRA members by soldiers. According to the Court's factsheet, it found a violation of Article 2 (right to life) because the operation could have been planned and controlled without the need to kill the suspects.

Citation: [ECHR-1995-18984](../sources/regions/europe.md#ECHR-1995-18984) ([https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57943](https://hudoc.echr.coe.int/eng?i=001-57943))

- Date: 1996-01-31
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Sub-Saharan Africa
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1044 (1996) concerning Sudan and the attempted assassination of President Mubarak in Addis Ababa.

Summary: On 31 January 1996, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1044 concerning Sudan and the attempted assassination of Egypt's President Mubarak in Addis Ababa on 26 June 1995. The Council condemned the assassination attempt as a terrorist act.

Citation: [UNSC1044](../sources/regions/sub-saharan-africa.md#UNSC1044) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/1044\(1996\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/1044(1996)))

## T038

- Date: 1996-04-24
- Place: Washington, D.C., United States
- Region: North America
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The US Congress enacted the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996.

Summary: On 24 April 1996, the US Congress enacted the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996. Its long title says it is an Act to deter terrorism, provide justice for victims and provide for an effective death penalty.

Citation: [US-AEDPA1996](../sources/regions/north-america.md#US-AEDPA1996) ([https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-104publ132/pdf/PLAW-104publ132.pdf](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-104publ132/pdf/PLAW-104publ132.pdf))

## T039

- Date: 1996-12-17
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN General Assembly adopted resolution 51/210, which established an Ad Hoc Committee on international terrorism conventions.

Summary: On 17 December 1996, the UN General Assembly adopted resolution 51/210, which established an Ad Hoc Committee on international terrorism conventions. The resolution also condemns terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable and reaffirms the 1994 Declaration (T034). The Terrorist Bombings Convention was adopted a year later (T040).

Citation: [UNGA51-210](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNGA51-210) ([https://undocs.org/A/RES/51/210](https://undocs.org/A/RES/51/210))

<a id="T040"></a>
## T040

- Date: 1997-12-15
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings was adopted.

Summary: On 15 December 1997, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention for the Suppression of Terrorist Bombings. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it creates universal jurisdiction over the intentional use of explosives or other lethal devices in or against public places with intent to kill, seriously injure or cause extensive destruction.

Citations:

- [CONV-BOMBINGS1997](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-BOMBINGS1997) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-9.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-9.pdf))
- [UNTC-XVIII](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNTC-XVIII) ([https://treaties.un.org/Pages/Treaties.aspx?id=18&subid=A&clang=_en](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/Treaties.aspx?id=18&subid=A&clang=_en))

## T041

- Date: 1998-04-10
- Place: Belfast, Northern Ireland, United Kingdom
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement was concluded.

Summary: On 10 April 1998, the Belfast (Good Friday) Agreement was concluded in Belfast. The UK Government page says it covered identity and citizenship and made commitments on decommissioning, security, policing and prisoners. It is the political settlement for Northern Ireland, where several of the UK emergency laws in CTA6 had applied.

Citation: [UK-GFA1998](../sources/regions/europe.md#UK-GFA1998) ([https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-belfast-agreement](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-belfast-agreement))

The Arab Convention for the Suppression of Terrorism was concluded under the League of Arab States.

Summary: On 22 April 1998, the Arab Convention for the Suppression of Terrorism was concluded in Cairo under the League of Arab States. It is the regional terrorism treaty for League members; its provisions are not summarized in CTA6 \[UNKNOWN\].

Citation: [ARAB-1998](../sources/regions/middle-east-north-africa.md#ARAB-1998) ([https://www.unodc.org/images/tldb-f/conv_arab_terrorism.en.pdf](https://www.unodc.org/images/tldb-f/conv_arab_terrorism.en.pdf))

## T043

- Date: 1998-08-13
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Sub-Saharan Africa
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1189 (1998) after the bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam.

Summary: On 13 August 1998, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1189 after the 7 August 1998 bombings in Nairobi and Dar-es-Salaam. The Council condemned the attacks, which it said claimed hundreds of lives, and called on States to support the investigations in Kenya, Tanzania and the United States.

Citation: [UNSC1189](../sources/regions/sub-saharan-africa.md#UNSC1189) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/1189\(1998\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/1189(1998)))

## T044

- Date: 1998-08-27
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Middle East/North Africa
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1192 (1998) on a trial in the Netherlands relating to the Pan Am 103 bombing.

Summary: On 27 August 1998, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1192 on a trial in the Netherlands relating to the Pan Am 103 bombing. It required Libya to ensure the two accused appeared in the Netherlands for trial and kept earlier sanctions in effect. It continues the sequence that began with resolution 731 (T031).

Citation: [UNSC1192](../sources/regions/middle-east-north-africa.md#UNSC1192) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/1192\(1998\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/1192(1998)))

- Date: 1999-10-15
- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1267 (1999), establishing a sanctions regime and committee concerning the Taliban.

Summary: On 15 October 1999, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1267, establishing a sanctions regime and committee concerning the Taliban. States were required from 14 November 1999 to apply measures including flight bans on aircraft operated by or for the Taliban. The regime was later extended and renamed (T104, T116), and its listings were challenged in court (T097).

Citation: [UNSC1267](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNSC1267) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/1267\(1999\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/1267(1999)))

- Place: New York, United States (UN Security Council)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: UN and international frameworks
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UN Security Council adopted resolution 1269 (1999) on international terrorism.

Summary: On 19 October 1999, the UN Security Council adopted resolution 1269 on international terrorism. It calls on States to implement the anti-terrorism conventions, to consider joining those they have not, and to cooperate with each other.

Citation: [UNSC1269](../sources/regions/global-un.md#UNSC1269) ([https://undocs.org/S/RES/1269\(1999\)](https://undocs.org/S/RES/1269(1999)))

<a id="T048"></a>
## T048

- Date: 1999-12-09
- Place: New York, United States (UN General Assembly)
- Region: Global/UN
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism was adopted.

Summary: On 9 December 1999, the UN General Assembly adopted the International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism. According to the UN Office of Counter-Terrorism, it requires States to prevent direct or indirect financing of terrorists, hold financiers liable, and identify, freeze and seize funds. Security Council resolution 1373 later made similar obligations binding on all States (T055).

Citations:

- [CONV-FINANCING1999](../sources/regions/global-un.md#CONV-FINANCING1999) ([https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-11.pdf](https://treaties.un.org/doc/db/Terrorism/english-18-11.pdf))

## T049

- Date: 2000-07-20
- Place: London, United Kingdom
- Region: Europe
- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

The UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2000.

Summary: On 20 July 2000, the UK Parliament enacted the Terrorism Act 2000. It covers proscribed organisations, terrorist property, terrorist investigations and terrorist offences across the UK. It followed the earlier Temporary Provisions Acts (T014, T027).

Citation: [UK-TA2000](../sources/regions/europe.md#UK-TA2000) ([https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2000/11/contents](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2000/11/contents))

- Theme: laws and treaties
- Status: `we-have-a-record`

Türkiye adopted the Anti-Terror Law (Terörle Mücadele Kanunu, Law No. 3713), published the same day in the Official Gazette.

Summary: On 12 April 1991, Türkiye adopted the Anti-Terror Law (Terörle Mücadele Kanunu, Law No. 3713), published the same day in the Official Gazette. Its article 1 (as amended in 2003) defines terror by reference to the use of force, violence or intimidation for listed aims, including changing the constitutional characteristics of the Republic. Parts of the law were later reviewed by the Constitutional Court (T216).

Japan enacted the Act on the Control of Organizations Which Have Committed Acts of Indiscriminate Mass Murder (Act No. 147 of 1999).

The Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment on merits, reparations and costs in C.P. et al. v. Peru (Serie C No. 52), concerning four Chilean nationals tried by a military tribunal with anonymous judges under Decree-Law No. 25.659, as described in the judgment.

Summary: On 30 May 1999, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights delivered its judgment on merits, reparations and costs in C.P. et al. v. Peru (Serie C No. 52). As described in the judgment, the case concerns four Chilean nationals tried by a military tribunal with anonymous judges under Decree-Law No. 25.659. The Court's ruling is not in the captured text \[UNKNOWN\].
